Few professions shape daily life as visibly as civil engineering, and that is what first drew me to it. Growing up fascinated by how bridges, roads, and skylines shape the way people live, travel, and connect, I chose civil engineering as the place where problem-solving and creativity meet to turn ideas into infrastructure that serves entire communities. I am originally from Bangladesh, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500. Through my studies and professional experience, I have become especially interested in translating complex technical requirements into clear, buildable plans that balance safety, efficiency, and cost, while working across different disciplines to keep projects moving steadily and on schedule. One of my favourite memories was taking my family on a road trip, where we crossed a bridge I had helped deliver and my youngest recognised a pedestrian crossing point on a concrete platform; watching that moment live in the real world confirmed for me how engineering can quietly influence how people move, connect, and experience.

That connection became especially personal during a community open day, when a family member visited the site and joked that it was “the site where I completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes.” Since then, my family has never passed a construction site without asking for an on-the-spot engineering commentary. In addition, I have completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in turning technical requirements into practical, buildable solutions that people can actually use. In one role, I needed to use a new tool and become familiar with a new subject area, and after a few months of focused effort I was contributing productively to the team’s work. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing progress, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the team keep projects moving. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas I have worked on before, and I value being able to help them move forward. Overall, I am eager to bring this combination of technical judgement, project focus, and practical delivery to a Civil Engineer role.

Few things are more satisfying than taking raw timber and shaping it into something lasting, useful, and beautifully made. That is what drew me to carpentry: the chance to combine creativity with practical problem-solving and to build spaces and furniture that become part of people’s daily lives. One of my clearest memories is bringing my family to see a community project I had helped build, only for my youngest relative to run straight to a bench I had made and proudly call it “our family bench.” That moment stayed with me because it captured exactly what I value in this trade: carpentry creates work that is not only practical, but also deeply personal, useful, and deeply rewarding. Originally from Peru, I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and across my work I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes.

My academic background gave me a structured way of approaching work, while my professional experience has shown me how much I enjoy seeing a space or project come together properly. In one role, I needed to use a new technique that the work required; within a couple of months I had learned it well enough to apply it independently in my own tasks. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put in place a practical workaround that reduced delays and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on before, and I value those exchanges because they keep work collaborative and dependable.

What keeps this career personal for me is the human side of it. One of my favourite memories is taking my family to see a community project I helped build, only for a younger relative to run straight to a bench I had made and proudly call it “our family bench.” That moment captured exactly why this trade matters to me. I am now eager to bring that same care, practical judgement, and commitment to well-made, useful work to a Carpenter role where I can contribute to projects that stand the test of time.

Order has always appealed to me most when many moving parts need to come together at the right time, which is why logistics became the right career path for me. I am originally from Spain, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. What first drew me in was the way logistics can turn complexity into a clear plan, helping people and products stay connected while operations stay on track. That connection became especially real on a family road trip when we unexpectedly passed one of the warehouses I had helped support during a peak shipping season; my family insisted we stop so I could show them “where all the planning happens,” and seeing them link my behind-the-scenes work to products arriving in stores made the profession feel even more rewarding.

My academic background gave me a structured way of approaching structured work, and I completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes that strengthened my interest in coordinating people, timelines, and priorities in a way that keeps operations moving. In one role, I had to use a method that was completely new to me; within a few weeks I was applying it confidently, and soon after I was the person colleagues came to when they needed someone to walk them through it. On another occasion, I noticed that the team was repeatedly losing time at the same handover point, so I introduced a simple adjustment to the process that reduced delays and saved time across the week. I also value working closely with colleagues: when teammates asked how I had approached a task or organised a process, I took time to walk them through it so they could apply it themselves.

Alongside this, I have completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing the importance of follow-through. In one drawn-out assignment, unexpected obstacles delayed progress more than once, but I stayed with it to completion and put in additional time where needed to see it through. Overall, I am eager to bring this combination of structured thinking, practical problem-solving, and steady coordination to a Logistics Coordinator role, contributing to reliable operations and a team that values clear planning and dependable service.
